1.explanation: This code imports the Carbon CSS and the React Grid components. The first <Grid> renders the default layout (24 px gutters). The second <Grid narrow> adds the class `bx--grid--narrow` to the container. Because the Carbon CSS shipped today does not include any rules for `.bx--grid--narrow`, you will see the grid still use the default left gutter but an oversized right gutter (no matching class to shrink it). That reproduces the misaligned 16 px gutter behavior shown in the documentation screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: When you try to use the “narrow” grid mode in `carbon-components-react` by passing the `narrow` prop to the `<Grid>` component, the rendered grid has an extra-large gutter on the right side (instead of equal 16 px gutters on both sides). In fact, the underlying CSS never defined styles for `.bx--grid--narrow`, so you get the default grid layout on the left and an unaccounted-for right gutter. This reproduces exactly the screenshot shown in the Carbon docs (with more space on the end gutter) but without any official CSS support for “narrow.”
